subject.title: Feature: trustedWebhooks for Discord — allow specific webhooks to trigger agent responses

question: Should Discord support guild-scoped trusted inbound webhook IDs, and if so may those messages map onto a configured user identity?
rationale: The allowlist is narrower than allowBots=true, but it creates a new trusted inbound authority surface and the optional user mapping crosses sender authorization and session-identity boundaries.

options.title: Approve Allowlist Without User Mapping
options.body: Allow selected webhook IDs to bypass the bot-message drop while preserving webhook/bot identity until a separate identity-mapping contract is approved.

options.title: Approve IdentityLinks Mapping
options.body: Permit mapping only through operator-configured identityLinks or an equivalent trusted-principal contract with tests proving it cannot bypass guild user authorization.

options.title: Decline Discord-Native Trusted Ingress
options.body: Keep Discord bot-message policy unchanged and direct external automation to the generic webhooks plugin or a separate extension design.

recommendation.title: Approve Allowlist Without User Mapping
recommendation.body: Allow selected webhook IDs to bypass the bot-message drop while preserving webhook/bot identity until a separate identity-mapping contract is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest adjacent inbound policy and trusted-metadata routing signal among the sampled history and timeline evidence.
